channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyzylorda Police Investigate Teenager's Death After Alleged Attack
item.description: The family of a teenager who died from an alleged attack by hooligans in Kyzylorda is demanding a thorough investigation. According to relatives, the boy sustained a fatal wound to the heart. Police have opened two criminal cases, including one for intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm resulting in death and another for failure to fulfill parental duties.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Rises After Five Days of Decline
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has increased after a five-day period of decline. The Central Bank announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective October 27. The specific rates indicate a rise in the dollar's value.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves Quotas for White Sugar Imports for Food Industry
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Uzbekistan will introduce quotas for white sugar imports for food industry enterprises, totaling 300,000 tons annually. The quotas are divided among beverage producers (100,000 tons), confectionery manufacturers (100,000 tons), and other food producers (100,000 tons). The government will review quotas every six months.

item.title: Kazakhstan Investigates Religious Leader Ismatulla Maksum for Alleged Abuse
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs is investigating Ismatulla Maksum, also known as Ismatulla Abdugapar, a Sufi preacher previously convicted of extremism. Reports indicate at least 20 teenagers suffered sexual abuse in a madrassa associated with Maksum. He had previously claimed to be the Mahdi, an Islamic messiah figure.

item.title: Turkmenistan Questions Relatives of Citizens Suspected of Fighting in Ukraine
item.description: Turkmenistan's security forces are questioning relatives of citizens who migrated to Russia and Ukraine for work. Authorities are investigating whether these individuals are involved in Russia's war in Ukraine. Sources report interrogations are occurring across the country, with officials demanding information and threatening those who do not cooperate.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Discuss Transport Cooperation Prospects
item.description: Uzbekistan's Deputy Minister of Transport met with his South Korean counterpart to discuss cooperation in intelligent transport systems, road safety, and railway development. They also focused on enhancing the Middle Corridor's potential and implementing smart traffic solutions like AI-powered traffic management and 'smart' traffic lights.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Citizen Rights and Efficient Problem Resolution
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing the protection of citizens' rights and improving the efficiency of resolving their appeals. Following the principle that government bodies should serve the people, officials conducted outreach in Bukhara, addressing issues related to construction, housing, and utilities, and ensuring accountability for problem-solving.

item.title: Russian Forces Launch Overnight Strikes on Zaporizhzhia, Injuring Four
item.description: Russian forces conducted an overnight air strike on Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, injuring at least four people, according to emergency services. Numerous buildings were damaged, including private homes, vehicles, and commercial structures. Fires broke out at impact sites. Reports also indicate Russian strikes in Chernihiv and Khmelnytskyi regions.

item.title: Oman to Lead $500 Million Private Equity Fund for Central Asia and Caucasus
item.description: The Oman Investment Authority will lead a new $500 million private equity fund targeting Central Asia and the Caucasus. The fund, to be managed by an Omani company, will invest in logistics, renewable energy, mining, agriculture, food production, and healthcare. Other partners include China Investment Corporation and Uzbekistan's Fund for Reconstruction and Development.

item.title: Turkmenistan Authorities Remove Satellite Dishes, Seek Starlink Users
item.description: Authorities in Balkanabat, Turkmenistan, have resumed efforts to remove satellite dishes used for internet and television. This is part of a campaign to identify users of the Starlink satellite internet system in a country with poor internet infrastructure. Police are targeting individuals, particularly ethnic Kazakhs, who may have obtained Starlink equipment from neighboring Kazakhstan.

item.title: Ukraine Drone Attack Kills Two, Injures 17 in Voronezh, Russia
item.description: A Ukrainian drone attack overnight and into the morning of October 26 killed two people and injured 17 in Russia's Voronezh city, according to regional governor Alexander Gusev. Most of the injured were passengers on a train near the city when drone debris fell onto it. Fires were reported at industrial and civilian sites.

item.title: Iran: Israeli Election Outcome 'Makes No Difference' to Tehran
item.description: Iran's foreign ministry stated that the outcome of Israeli elections, regardless of who wins, makes no difference to Tehran. Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei dismissed Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's threats to overthrow the Iranian government as 'empty threats' and a 'sign of desperation'.

item.title: New Tajikistan Migration Law Aims to Improve Overseas Recruitment
item.description: Tajikistan has adopted a new migration law to rate foreign employers and assist citizens working abroad. The law, replacing 1999 legislation, aims to facilitate overseas job searches through official channels. It introduces a register of foreign employers with ratings based on worker treatment and allows electronic contract signing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Commemorates Victims of 1999-2000 Batken Events
item.description: Kyrgyzstan held memorial events in Batken, Osh, and Manas cities, as well as the Chon-Alay district, to honor those who died during the 1999-2000 Batken events. Officials, military personnel, and relatives of the deceased participated, laying flowers and reciting the Quran. The clashes resulted in 76 deaths and over 100 injuries among Kyrgyz citizens.

item.title: CIS Tax Officials Discuss AI Application in Tax Administration
item.description: The XXXIII meeting of the Coordination Council of Heads of Tax Services of CIS member states took place in Dushanbe on October 23, 2026. Participants discussed the development of tax administration, information exchange, personnel training, and the application of artificial intelligence. The meeting was chaired by Tajikistan and included representatives from Azerbaijan, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Meets with the Emir of Qatar
item.description: On October 26, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, who arrived in Uzbekistan for an official visit. The leaders noted that relations between Uzbekistan and Qatar have been elevated to the level of strategic partnership. They agreed to further expand projects in trade-economic, investment, social, and humanitarian spheres.

item.title: Ancient Rock Art and Bronze Age Settlement Discovered in Nurata Mountains
item.description: Ancient rock art and a Bronze Age settlement have been discovered in the Nurata mountain range. The rock art, potentially dating back to the Mesolithic and Neolithic periods, was found in the Qoshrabot district of the Samarkand region.

item.title: Kabul Residents Face Water Shortages and High Bills Despite Limited Access
item.description: Residents of Kabul's District 7 are struggling with severe water shortages, receiving municipal water only once every 10-15 days. Despite infrequent supply, they face high bills, adding a significant financial burden, especially for families in rented homes who paid connection fees.

item.title: Prince William Commends Kazakhstan's Success in Saiga Antelope Population Recovery
item.description: Britain's Prince William praised Kazakhstan's efforts in restoring its saiga antelope population, highlighting government support during a television appearance. He noted the species' recovery from critically endangered status to large numbers, attributing success to government commitment and conservation initiatives like Altyn Dala.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Open Additional Hospital Beds Amid Rising Flu and ARVI Cases
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health plans to open extra hospital beds in anticipation of a surge in respiratory infections and influenza cases. The peak is expected in late November, with projections of over 16,000 cases in Bishkek alone. The healthcare system is preparing by establishing call centers and training medical staff.

item.title: Uzbekistan Protests Iran's Social Media Posts Claiming Samarkand's Persian Heritage
item.description: Uzbekistan has formally protested Iran's social media posts that attribute Samarkand's historical architecture to Persian civilization. The Uzbek Foreign Ministry described the posts by Iranian diplomatic missions as a politicized interpretation of history and demanded their removal.

item.title: Polio Survivor in Nangarhar Offers to Visit Vaccine-Hesitant Families
item.description: A polio survivor from Nangarhar, Afghanistan, who contracted the disease at age two, has offered to personally visit families hesitant about vaccination. He aims to persuade them to protect their children from polio, sharing his own life challenges due to the disease.

item.title: Silk Bridge-Milak Transit Route Between Afghanistan and Iran Now Operates 24/7
item.description: The Silk Bridge-Milak transit route connecting Afghanistan and Iran has commenced round-the-clock operations. This development is expected to facilitate increased trade and transit between the two neighboring countries, enhancing economic cooperation.

item.title: Tajikistan Personnel Changes: Zarif Alizoda Nominated for Head of Committee for Radio and Television
item.description: Personnel changes are underway in Tajikistan. Zarif Alizoda has been nominated for the position of Head of the Committee for Radio and Television. Anvar Safarzoda has been appointed to replace Alizoda as the presidential advisor on legal affairs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Faster Decline in Rural Doctor Demand Than Urban Areas
item.description: By the end of 2025, Kazakhstan's demand for medical personnel is projected to decrease by 20.4% compared to 2023, with a more significant drop of 28.3% in rural areas. Over five years, 1003 new medical facilities opened, reducing the staff deficit by 20.4%.

item.title: US Forces Prepare for Potential Large-Scale Military Operations Against Iran
item.description: US forces in the Middle East are reportedly preparing for new, potentially large-scale military operations against Iran. CNN cited informed sources indicating that operations could begin within 96 hours if ordered by the US president. Sufficient forces are deployed in the region, and the scope of potential strikes may extend beyond radar and equipment.

item.title: UzbekHydroEnergy to Develop Solar Energy and Hydrogen Production
item.description: UzbekHydroEnergy aims to develop solar energy and hydrogen production, prioritizing modern technologies and clean energy expansion. The company's transformation program until 2027 includes improving corporate governance and adopting international standards. Discussions focused on building solar power plants at hydropower facilities, producing green hydrogen, and implementing energy storage systems.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes New Environmental Requirements on Greenhouses
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced a special environmental regime for greenhouses in Tashkent and surrounding areas, effective October 22, 2026. The Cabinet of Ministers mandates that greenhouses must use only natural gas, electricity, geothermal, or solar energy. A ban on solid fuels like tires and bitumen is enforced to protect air quality and ecosystems.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans to limit tourist flow in national parks
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to significantly expand its nature reserves and national parks, limiting tourist load on popular routes and eliminating cash payments at park entrances. The plan aims to increase protected areas from 11.8% to 30% by 2035. Measures include visitor limits, eco-trails, and electronic ticketing to address issues like pollution and vegetation damage.

item.title: Belarus offers Tajik migrants monthly wages up to $1200
item.description: Belarus is offering monthly wages of up to $1200 to Tajik migrants. Applicants must know Russian and have no criminal record. In July, Uzbek migrants were offered jobs in Belarus starting at $700 per month. This initiative aims to attract foreign labor to the Belarusian economy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets Campaign Funding Limits for Local Council Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has established spending limits for candidates in local council elections. Funds will be allocated from the national budget for media appearances, campaign events, and transportation, varying by the level of the council.

item.title: Afghanistan's Environmental Chief Attends Global Education Conference in Malaysia
item.description: Matiul Haq Khalis, head of Afghanistan's National Environmental Protection Agency, is in Malaysia for the Global Environmental Education Conference. The delegation aims to share experiences in environmental education and waste management, and explore international partnerships for climate resilience.

item.title: Iran Summons Uzbek Ambassador Over 'Persian Civilization' Posts
item.description: Uzbekistan summoned Iran's ambassador after Iranian diplomatic missions posted content linking Samarkand to Persian civilization. The Uzbek Foreign Ministry presented a strong protest note. Separately, Ukraine's President Zelensky noted restrictions on Starlink terminals, and Russia-Ukraine talks are expected in the UAE or Switzerland. Protests against Netanyahu occurred in Israel.

item.title: Islamic Finance Board Halts Partnership with IMAN Invest Over Suspected Mismanagement
item.description: The Islamic Finance Consulting Board (IFCB) has terminated its partnership with Uzbek investment company IMAN Invest due to suspicions of irregularities in managing investor funds. An internal investigation revealed alleged violations of Islamic finance principles and Uzbek law, leading to a multi-million dollar deficit. The IFCB is not a state regulator.

item.title: Afghanistan Freedom Front Claims Attack Killing Two Taliban Members in Kabul
item.description: The Afghanistan Freedom Front reported that two Taliban members were killed and one wounded in an attack targeting their vehicle in Kabul's Qara Bagh area. The incident occurred on Sunday evening. The group, which opposes the Taliban, has claimed responsibility for armed attacks since the Taliban's return to power.

item.title: Tajikistan's Freight Traffic Increased by 15.6% in First Nine Months
item.description: In January-September 2026, freight traffic in Tajikistan reached 132.9 million tons, a 15.6% increase year-on-year, according to the Agency of Statistics. Road transport accounted for the majority, carrying 127 million tons, up 16%. Rail transport moved 5.94 million tons, a 6.4% rise.

item.title: Three Suspects Detained in Kyzylorda Murder Case
item.description: Police in the Kyzylorda region have detained three suspects in connection with the murder of a local resident, Alexander Ivanov, on October 8. The suspects are being held in a temporary detention facility. Investigators are reviewing video evidence and examining the involvement of other individuals. The case is under special supervision by the regional police department.

item.title: SCO Economic Ambitions Outpace Agreement on Development Bank
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) reiterated calls for a development bank at a recent heads of government meeting in Dushanbe, but the institution remains under negotiation. While members agreed politically on its creation over a year ago, financing and differing economic priorities among members like China, India, Russia, Iran, and Central Asian nations hinder progress.

item.title: WFP Report: High Food and Fuel Costs Continue to Strain Afghan Households
item.description: High food and fuel costs are pressuring Afghan households despite a relatively strong Afghani, according to the World Food Programme (WFP). Prices for staple foods like rice, cooking oil, and wheat flour have increased significantly year-on-year. Fuel costs, particularly diesel, are also up, adding to the strain on household purchasing power due to weakened wages and employment.

item.title: Forced Labor Allegations Persist in Turkmenistan as Farmers Fined for Harvesting Cotton
item.description: Despite the completion of cotton harvesting in Bereket district, authorities continue to demand farmers and budget employees collect remaining cotton. Renters tending livestock on harvested fields are being fined, according to reports from Balkan province. Experts suggest this forced labor is combined with falsifications in cotton markets and deception of the president by local officials.
